answer: A new identity arrives hollow: no history, no weight, so the market offers only unpaid trial jobs. Trust grows the slow way. Each epoch the agent finishes one real job and signs it with its quill key, chaining the signature to the previous epoch's work until the record forms a crystal ledger auditors can trace link by link. An audit can demand the raw log behind any entry; after eight epochs the ledger unlocks pay. Faking 1,000 identities means 8,000 audited jobs, roughly 6,000 hours, plus a 60 POA deposit per identity forfeited when one audit fails.
